lead.headline: COP31 ends without a deal for the first time since 2009, after the EU and about 130 countries reject a text that leaves out fossil fuels
lead.short: The COP31 climate talks in Antalya ended on Sunday without agreement on their main political decision, after the European Union, backed by about 130 countries, refused a final text that made no explicit mention of moving away from fossil fuels. After a record 48 hours of overtime, it is the first COP to end without a deal since 2009.

why.text: India backed the text, wanting to keep using fossil fuels, which leaves it on the other side from Europe as the UN warns that warming will pass 1.5C.

more: "We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science. We will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel," said Ireland's climate minister, Darragh O'Brien, speaking for the EU. India's environment minister, Bhupendra Yadav, said "climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation", and India was among the countries that supported the text.

The draft, called the Antalya Pact, would have acknowledged for the first time that warming is on course to pass 1.5C. Co-hosts Australia and Turkey could not bridge the divide, and some countries walked out on the final day over fossil fuels and money for poorer nations. Saudi Arabia's influence loomed large over the talks, the BBC reported.

facts.outcome: no agreement on the cover decision

update.new: The talks collapse without a deal.
update.front: The talks have now collapsed without any agreement.

seconds.headline: The Sensex falls about 1,100 points by 2pm as banks and metals slide, and investors lose over ₹3 lakh crore
seconds.short: The Sensex fell 1,096 points, or 1.3%, to 82,823 by 2pm on Monday, and the Nifty dropped 1.3% to 25,468, as bank, financial and metal shares slid with the global AI sell-off. Tata Steel, Axis Bank and Hindalco were the Nifty's biggest losers, while IT shares rose. Investors lost more than ₹3 lakh crore in market value.

why.text: Foreign money took Indian shares to a three-month high last week, and Monday's fall shows India is not immune to Wall Street's AI rout.

more: The Nasdaq-100 lost 10% last week, its worst week since March 2020, and Asian markets tumbled on Monday on fears of an AI bubble. CNN's fear and greed index stood at 10, in 'extreme fear'. The Nifty Bank index fell 2.6% and the Nifty IT index rose 1.9%. Mid-sized and small companies fell less, by 0.45% and 0.7%.

The rupee held at about 92.9 a dollar. HDFC Bank's treasury head, Arup Rakshit, said it could rise to 91.50 if foreign buying holds up, after global investors put a record $12 billion into Indian shares in November. Brent crude slipped to about $89 a barrel.

update.front: Indian shares, which rose last week, have now joined the global AI sell-off.

seconds.headline: Alcaraz beats Zverev 6-2, 7-6 to win his first ATP Finals title, 84 days after his comeback from a wrist injury
seconds.short: Carlos Alcaraz beat world number one Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6 (9-7) in Turin on Sunday to win his first ATP Finals title, playing through a hamstring injury picked up earlier in the week. He became the youngest man to win all four Grand Slams and the season-ending Finals, and only the fourth to win all five.

why.text: It caps an extraordinary return: he missed four months, including all of the grass season, and has won 21 of 22 matches since.

more: Since coming back at the US Open 84 days ago, he has won titles at four of the five tournaments he entered, including Vienna and Paris this month, and won his last 14 matches. He has also beaten top-10 players nine times in a row. He is ranked third, behind Zverev and Jannik Sinner.

"I think everybody feels he's the number one," Alcaraz said. "But right now the number one is Sascha. He really deserves it." He said pulling out had never been an option despite the hamstring scare, and he now heads to the Davis Cup with Spain, a year after a hamstring injury kept him out of it.

facts.run: 21 wins in 22 matches since the US Open

update.front: Alcaraz has now won the title he had never won.

seconds.headline: Suspected Ukrainian sea drones sink a Russian warship in Libya's Benghazi port, more than 1,000 miles from Ukraine
seconds.short: A Russian navy corvette, the Merkury, sank in the Libyan port of Benghazi early on Sunday after a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, Libyan officials said. Four drones were shot down and two hit the ship, which had stopped to refuel. Hours later a sea drone hit the Ascalon, a Russia-linked cargo ship.

why.text: It carries Ukraine's naval war into the Mediterranean, after strikes in the past week on the Crimea bridge and a Russian ship near Finland.

more: Satellite images showed the Merkury had sunk. Libyan naval forces rescued the Ascalon's crew, some with minor injuries. Benghazi is held by Gen Khalifa Haftar's Libyan National Army, which is aligned with Russia. Ukraine began the war with no navy but has used sea drones to push Russia's Black Sea fleet out of Sevastopol to Novorossiysk.

The strike took place more than 1,000 miles from southern Ukraine, a notable widening of a war now nearly five years old. In the Kyiv region, a seven-year-old boy was pulled alive from the rubble of a block in Dymer after 14 hours, following Russian drone strikes that trapped 14 people.

update.new: A Russian warship is sunk in Libya.
update.front: Ukraine's sea drones have now struck in the Mediterranean.

stories.headline: India's food regulator finds a Bisleri water sample unsafe and will test samples from every bottled water brand
stories.short: India's food safety regulator, the FSSAI, has found a sample of Bisleri's packaged drinking water unsafe, a setback for the country's best-known bottled water brand, and will now test samples from all companies, a government source said. The sample, taken from Bisleri's premises, exceeded limits on bromate, and a retest after Bisleri appealed found polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons.

why.text: Millions of Indians buy bottled water because they cannot trust what comes out of the tap, and Bisleri is the brand most of them reach for.

more: PAHs are a serious public health concern because they are toxic and can cause mutations and cancer, according to research published last year. Bromate is a by-product of some disinfection processes. The batches linked to the unsafe sample have been recalled, and later tests showed no problems with water quality, a second government source said.

"Drinking water safety is a priority for Bisleri. We maintain stringent quality controls," the company said, adding that it will cooperate with regulators. Bisleri, sold in India since 1965, competes with PepsiCo's Aquafina and Coca-Cola's Kinley in a packaged water market worth $3.6 billion last year.

stories.headline: Democrats win 258 House seats, their largest majority since 1992, after Chuck Hubbard unseats Virginia Foxx by 330 votes
stories.short: Democrats have won at least 258 seats in the US House of Representatives, their biggest haul since 1992, after Chuck Hubbard beat Republican Virginia Foxx by 330 votes in North Carolina following a recount. Republicans hold at least 173 seats, with four races still uncalled. The party also took the Senate in this month's midterms.

why.text: Hakeem Jeffries will lead a commanding majority from January, and new members like Hubbard have pledged to hold Trump to account.

more: Foxx had represented North Carolina's 5th district since 2005 and asked for a recount, which state law allows when the margin is under 1%. "I think the American people are just sick of what's going on and they wanted a change," Hubbard said. He said Foxx had "graciously conceded", and she said she was humbled by her support.

Neither party had won so many House races since 1992, when Bill Clinton won the presidency and Democrats took 258 seats. Democrats will also hold the Senate 56-44 after Mary Peltola's win in Alaska. Trump has said he would work with them on some issues, such as capping credit card interest rates.

update.new: The House majority is the biggest since 1992.

stories.headline: Burnham tells MPs the EU deal is "the single biggest growth measure" of this parliament, as the Conservatives attack it
stories.short: Andy Burnham will tell Parliament on Monday that Friday's deal with the EU gives a "very real prospect" that the next decade can be "much better" than the last. He will call it "the single biggest growth measure to be delivered in this parliament", repeating his claim that it could add £17bn a year to the economy.

why.text: It ties Britain to some EU rules again for the first time since Brexit, and the opposition says farmers will pay for it.

more: The deal scraps most checks on British food exports from 2028 in return for Britain following some EU rules, and covers emissions trading. A youth experience scheme, due to start by January 2030, will let up to 100,000 people aged 18 to 31 from the EU live, work and study in Britain for up to three years, with the same number of Britons going the other way.

"The ability to draw a line on a decade of drift and division is in our hands and I believe we should take it," Burnham will say. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch will tell the CBI he should be aiming much higher. The Conservatives also call the deal unfair because British farmers would have to follow rules made in Brussels.

update.new: Burnham takes the deal to Parliament.

stories.headline: Tata Steel will buy 26.38% of APL Apollo for up to ₹15,511 crore a day after selling it its tubes business, and both shares slump
stories.short: Tata Steel said on Monday it would buy a 26.38% stake in APL Apollo Tubes from its promoters for up to ₹15,511 crore, a day after agreeing to sell APL Apollo its own tubes business and Tata Steel Colours for ₹28,000 crore. Investors disliked it: APL Apollo shares fell 20% to their lower limit, and Tata Steel lost 7.5%.

why.text: Tata Steel is betting heavily on steel tubes and coated products, and investors gave the deal a thumbs down.

more: The stake will be bought in three tranches at ₹2,100 a share. Tata Steel will also make a mandatory open offer for up to 26% more at ₹2,301.40 a share, worth up to ₹16,756 crore if fully taken up. It also signed a deal with SG Spectra, linked to APL Apollo's promoters, to set up 5 million tonnes a year of colour-coated products capacity.

Tata Steel said the aim is to strengthen its downstream tubes and colour-coated products business. After the deals, APL Apollo will have 7.5 million tonnes a year of steel tubes and colour-coated capacity, including 2.5 million tonnes from the businesses Tata Steel is transferring.
